title: Strong continuous real dual
statement: Let $V$ be a real vector space over $\mathbf R$ [def-weil-field], with a topology for which addition $V\times V\to V$ and scalar multiplication $\mathbf R\times V\to V$ are continuous. Define its strong continuous dual by $V'_b=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf R,\mathrm{cont}}(V,\mathbf R)$: its elements are continuous functions $u:V\to\mathbf R$ with $u(v+w)=u(v)+u(w)$ and $u(av)=a\,u(v)$, and its vector operations are pointwise. A subset $S\subseteq V$ is bounded if for every neighbourhood $U$ of $0$ there is $r>0$ such that $S\subseteq aU$ for every real $a$ with $|a|\geq r$. Endow $V'_b$ with the topology of uniform convergence on these bounded subsets: a neighbourhood subbasis at $0$ consists of $\{u\mid u(S)\subseteq W\}$ for bounded $S\subseteq V$ and neighbourhoods $W$ of $0$ in $\mathbf R$; neighbourhoods at other functionals are translates.
